_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Reliability-Centered Maintenance (RCM) Task Definition Report
summary: The RCM Task Definition Report provides detailed procedures of each maintenance task so a decision can be made on the appropriate maintenance level to perform it.
use_relationship:
The Reliability-Centered Maintenance (RCM) Task Definition Report provides detailed procedures of each task such that a decision can be made as to the appropriate maintenance level to perform the task.
This Data Item Description (DID) contains the format, content, preparation instructions and intended use information for the data product resulting from the work task described in 5.1.10 of MIL-STD-3034A.
This DID is related to DI-PSSS-80979BA, RCM Master Systems and Subsystems Index (MSSI); DI-PSSS-80994B, RCM Functional Block Diagram (FBD); DI-PSSS-80981B, RCM Functional Failure Analysis (FFA) Report; DI-PSSS-80983B, RCM Additional Functionally Significant Item (AFSI) Selection Report; DI-PSSS-80982B, RCM Functionally Significant Items (FSI) Index; DI-PSSS-80980B, RCM Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA) Report; DI-PSSS-80984B, RCM Decision Logic Tree Analysis (LTA) with Supporting Rationale and Justification Report; DI-PSSS-80985B, RCM Servicing and Lubrication Analysis (SLA) Report; DI-PSSS-80989B, RCM Inactive Equipment Maintenance (IEM) Requirement Analysis Report; DI-PSSS-81829A, RCM Corrective Maintenance (CM) Development Report; DI-PSSS-80986B, RCM Maintenance Requirements Index (MRI); DI-PSSS-80987B, RCM Procedure Validation Report; DI-PSSS-80990A, RCM Documentation Control Sheet.
This DID supersedes DI-SESS-80988A.
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Reference Documents.
preparation_instructions.content: The applicable issue of the documents cited herein, including their approval dates and dates of any applicable amendments, notices, and revisions, shall be as specified in the contract.

preparation_instructions.title: Format.
preparation_instructions.content: The task definition report shall be in a format similar to that of the sample form of Figure 1 of this DID.

preparation_instructions.title: Content.
preparation_instructions.content: The task definition report shall contain all the information specified in the sample form of Figure 1 of this DID and as specified in MIL-STD-3034A, paragraph 5.1.10.2.

children.title: Block 1. ESWBS Number.
children.content: Enter the Expanded Ship Work Breakdown Structure (ESWBS) entry from block 1 of the Maintenance Requirement Index (MRI).

children.title: Block 2. Nomenclature.
children.content: Enter the nomenclature of the item upon which the task is performed from block 2 of the MRI.

children.title: Block 3. Ship Class.
children.content: Enter ship class from block 3 of the MRI.

children.title: Block 4. Prepared By.
children.content: Enter the analyst's name and the date.

children.title: Block 5. Reviewed By.
children.content: Enter the first level reviewer's name and the date.

children.title: Block 6. Approved By.
children.content: Reserved for the Maintenance Coordinating Activity approval signature and the date.

children.title: Block 7. Revision.
children.content: Identify the revision level of the task definition report and enter e.g. "ORIGINAL", "A", "B", "C", etc., sequentially as applicable and the date.

children.title: Block 8. Equipment Nomenclature.
children.content: Enter the nomenclature of the item upon which the task is performed from block 9 of the MRI.

children.title: Block 9. Quantity Installed.
children.content: Enter the installed quantity of the item on which this task must be performed.

children.title: Block 10. Reference.
children.content: Enter the reference data listed in block 12 of the MRI, as applicable.

children.title: Block 11. Maintenance Requirement Description (Task).
children.content: Enter the task(s) description(s) from block 10 of the MRI. If applicable, several tasks from the MRI shall be combined into a single maintenance requirement description.

children.title: Block 12. Safety Precautions.
children.content: All required safety precautions shall be included in this block. The first entry in this area shall identify general safety requirement documentation by publication number and volume as specified in MIL-STD-3034A, paragraph 5.1.10.2. Also, the first letter of the first word in each safety precaution shall contain a capitalized letter.

children.title: Additional Warnings.
children.content: Additional, more specific warnings shall follow when applicable and shall be listed in the order in which they appear in the procedure. These warnings will also immediately precede the applicable step.

children.title: Additional Warnings Requiring the Use of Additional Personnel.
children.content: For those actions which require additional personnel because of safety regulations, the phrase "Do not work alone" shall be added to the applicable safety precaution; e.g. "Voltage dangerous to life are present when interlock switch is bypassed. Do not work alone." Appropriate personnel and man-hours must be added to the maintenance requirement when this statement is used.

children.title: Submarine Applications.
children.content: When Submarine Safety (SUBSAFE) boundaries are to be violated, the statement, "Ensure compliance with a SUBAFE Re-entry Control Procedures of NAVSEA 0924-062-0010 and COMFLTFORCOMINST 4790.3, Volume V, as applicable," shall appear in block 12. When Scope of Certification items are impacted, the statement "Ensure compliance with DSS-SOC Re-entry Control Procedures of NAVSEA SS800-AG-MAN-010/P-9290 (with the appropriate DSS-SOC Notebook)" shall appear in this area.

children.title: Cleaning Solvents.
children.content: When cleaning solvents are involved, the following standard safety precaution shall appear in block 12, "Avoid prolonged contact with, or inhalation of, cleaning solvents. Avoid use near open flame and provide adequate ventilation."

children.title: Block 13. Periodicity.
children.content: Enter the periodicity of this task from block 13 of the Maintenance Requirements Index (MRI) form. For PMS MRCs, enter a two-segment code; e.g., "4416 Q-2", "7211 Q-1", and "2331 R-1". The first segment is the ESWBS/MIP series code which will be provided by the applicable MCA. The second segment is the task periodicity. Identify MRCs applicable to more than one MIP series and enter each MIP series into block 13. The ESWBS and Class Maintenance Plan (CMP) maintenance requirement periodicity shall be entered in months.

children.title: Block 14. PMS MRC Rates and Man-Hours.
children.content: Identify and enter, by rating and rate, the number of persons required to perform the maintenance requirement and the man-hours required for each person. Additional entries in this area shall be included as follows:

children.title: The Navy Enlisted Classification (NEC) shall be entered if special skills are required.
When both NEC and rates are important to the task, both shall be included; e.g., GM2, with the NEC 0876 listed beneath the rate.
children.content: NECs shall not be in parentheses; multiple NECs shall be separated by a slash (/).

children.title: Titles for officers shall be the first entry in the block when applicable; e.g., "Damage Control Assistant (DCA)", "Electronic Material Officer (EMO)", "Engineering Officer (Eng. Off.)."

In cases where more than one rating is required, ratings shall be listed after the officers descending by rate within each rating category; e.g., "Eng. Off.", "Electrician's Mate First Class (EM1)", and "Machinist's Mate Second Class (MM2)."

When more than one person is required for a particular rate, the appropriate number shall precede the rate; e.g., "2 Operations Specialists First Class (2 OS1)", "2 Sonar Technicians Surface First Class (2 STG1), and 3 Electronics Technicians Second Class (3 ET2)."
children.content: When more than one person of the same rate are required and their time requirements are not equal, each person shall be listed separately. When additional personnel are required because of safety regulations, the rate and number of such personnel shall also be included.

children.title: In cases where either of two similar ratings can be assigned the work on an MRC, both ratings shall be listed and separated by a slash; e.g., "Fire Control Technician First Class (FC1)/Electronics Technician First Class (ET1)", "Gunner's Mate Second Class (GM2)/Gunner's Mate Missiles Second Class (GMM2)."
Calendar periodicity and "R" periodicity MRCs shall include the necessary rates to perform the maintenance.
children.content: Inactive Equipment Maintenance (IEM) procedural MRCs shall also include rates. MRCs with a U periodicity shall include rates when so directed by the MCA.

children.title: Man-hours (M/H) (converted to hours and tenths of an hour) shall be entered immediately to the right of each rate in the RATES area.
children.content: When the M/H figure is less than one hour, a zero shall appear before the tenths of an hour portion; for example, "0.1" and "0.4." When an officer is required, no M/H shall be assigned for that person.

children.title: The time entered shall indicate the M/H required for each rate as if they were performing their tasks independently.
children.content: When more than one of the same rating and rate are required and their time requirements are equal, the M/H will be the sum of their time requirements. When more than one person of the same rating and rate are required and their requirements are not equal, each person shall be listed separately.

children.title: Equipment warm-up time of up to 30 minutes shall be included in the assigned M/H, block 14.
children.content: Warm-up time in excess of 30 minutes, as well as periods not requiring maintenance technician intervention (i.e. charge batteries for 24 hours) shall not be included unless the maintainer is required for constant observance.

children.title: "Make ready" and "put away" times shall not be included in block 14.

When a technical procedure from another document, including another MRC, is referred to in the procedure area and only a portion of the maintenance procedure is to be accomplished, time required to do that portion shall be included in the M/H of the person accomplishing the task of the subject task procedure.
children.content: However, if the referenced procedure is an entire scheduled-related MRC, the M/H of that MRC shall not be included.

children.title: Block 15. Total M/H.
children.content: Enter the sum of the man-hours from the M/H block 14.

children.title: Block 16. Elapsed Time.
children.content: The entry in this area shall indicate the elapsed time, in clock hours and tenths of an hour, from start to finish of the maintenance procedure. The time involved for preparation to accomplish the task and cleanup time upon completion shall not be included.

children.title: Block 17. Tools, Parts, Materials, Test Equipment (TPME).
children.content: Enter, identify and numerically list TPME for the following categories as specified in MIL-STD-3034A, paragraph 5.1.10.2.r:

children.title: Block 18. Maintenance Procedure.
children.content: Identify and enter the step-by-step instructions needed to accomplish the maintenance requirement. Illustrations and figures shall be included, when applicable, to clarify content.

children.title: Block 19. Ships Crew.
children.content: Enter a "Y" to signify a yes answer and an "N" to signify a no answer to the question, "Can this task be done by the ship's crew without external skills, materials, tools, equipment?"

children.title: Block 20. Level (Of Maintenance).
children.content: Enter the lowest maintenance echelon at which this task can be done and enter the level recommended at which the maintenance requirement should be done.

children.title: Block 21. Location.
children.content: Enter the compartment number of the space(s) where the item(s) are located for ships. For all other applications, enter nomenclature to uniquely identify item(s) location.

children.title: Block 22. Serial Number.
children.content: Enter a four-segment serial number as follows:

children.title: Segment 1 - Enter the developing organization abbreviation followed by a slant (/).
Segment 2 - For developers, enter the development authorization number followed by a slant (/); for other development activities assign a development number followed by a slant (/).
Segment 3 - Enter the number 124 indicating the task definition form followed by a slant (/).
Segment 4 - Enter the ESWBS number from block 1.
